stories.title: Mayo Clinic AI detects pancreatic cancer up to 3 years before diagnosis in landmark validation study
stories.synopsis: A Mayo Clinic AI model called REDMOD helps specialists spot pancreatic cancer on routine abdominal CT scans up to three years before clinical diagnosis. In a study of nearly 2,000 scans that were originally read as normal, it identified 73% of the prediagnostic cancers about 16 months ahead of diagnosis, nearly double the rate of specialists working without AI. The team is now moving the work into clinical testing, which is hopeful news for earlier treatment of a very hard-to-catch cancer.

stories.title: AI is changing cancer treatment — and a new breakthrough shows just how far we've come
stories.synopsis: Researchers are using AI to understand cancer in far more detail than was possible a decade ago, moving toward treatments matched to the genetic makeup of each person's tumor. One example is the National Cancer Institute's PERCEPTION tool, which reads gene activity in individual cancer cells to predict whether certain drugs might work. The article is clear that lab and patient testing still come next, but it sees encouraging signs for more personalized care.

stories.title: AI Forecasts Heart Patients' Survival Slightly Better Than Doctors
stories.synopsis: In a study of 27,382 heart patients in the UK and US, an AI program measured heart function from scans in just three to four seconds. Its numbers also tracked which patients later survived slightly better than the doctors' own readings. Doctors still came out ahead for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which points to AI and clinicians working well as a team.
